text:
- Breathing that gets slow and shallow, or any trouble breathing
- Lips that turn blue or gray
- A [seizure](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/170920118/active-seizure) after they took too much or nobody knows how much, or one on a normal dose that goes past 5 minutes
- Collapsing, or not waking when you shake them and say their name
- Getting harder to wake by the minute
- A forehead that's dangerously hot to the touch, not just sweaty
- Muscles gone rigid, or a fever along with jerking they can't stop (clonus)
- No sleep for days
- Sudden weakness on one side of the body, or losing the ability to speak
- Not being able to walk normally
- Wetting or soiling themselves
- The feeling that their brain is damaged, when they can't do [the brain checks](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/170920118/my-brain-feels-damaged) or are quickly getting worse at them
- [Chest pain](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/170920118/chest-pain-and-injury) that's severe or getting worse, or that spreads into an arm or the jaw
- Chest pain that came on with hard movement, or that comes with sweating or shortness of breath, or makes them feel faint
- A serious injury, like uncontrolled bleeding or a possible head or spine injury
- Vomiting that won't stop
- Blood in their vomit or stool
- Being badly dried out: not peeing for hours, or dizzy when they stand up
- Bad stomach pain
- [Concerning symptoms](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/170920118/how-to-check-for-ss) after they took an MAOI, which keeps serotonin from breaking down (some older antidepressants, or the harmalas in ayahuasca and Syrian rue seeds), with something that raises serotonin, like MDMA or most antidepressants
reader: a friend with someone who took something a few hours ago and is getting worse, reading the list to decide whether to call an ambulance

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone? Is each mechanism explained by what it does in the reader's experience (dopamine "for motivation (by showing us what is important to pay attention to)"; DeltaFosB "preventing that learning from really clicking"), not by where it sits or what it looks like ("a chemical blanket", "the slower one underneath")? (E375)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
